title: A Singapore Where Every Child Can Flourish: Creating Safe Environments
what_it_is: A Singapore Where Every Child Can Flourish: Creating Safe Environments

sections.label: MUIS mosque safeguarding framework
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes MUIS developing a common safeguarding framework across mosques, strengthening staff training, clarifying reporting procedures and helping children, parents and educators seek help.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is particularly important for young children and children with developmental or communication difficulties who might find it harder to recognise abuse and to describe what has happened or seek help.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the recent announcement by the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura or MUIS) that it will develop a common safeguarding framework across mosques in Singapore and that it will strengthen training for staff and volunteers, clarify reporting and escalation procedures, and help children, parents and educators recognise concerns and seek help.

sections.label: Common minimum safeguarding standard
sections.summary: The passage asks whether organisations routinely working with children could adopt a common minimum safeguarding standard built around three layers of protection.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could organisations that routinely work with children adopt a common minimum standard of safeguarding built around three layers of protection?

sections.label: Bullying victimisation and MOE review
sections.summary: The passage states longitudinal research links victimisation to mental health and social difficulties persisting into adulthood, and welcomes MOE's Comprehensive Action Review Against Bullying.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Longitudinal research shows that victimisation is associated with increased risks of mental health and social difficulties that can persist into adulthood.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I therefore welcome the Ministry of Education's (MOE's) Comprehensive Action Review Against Bullying.

sections.label: Children's lived experience of safety
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the next step could be complementing this with systematic attention to children's lived experience of safety.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the next step be to complement this with systematic attention to children's lived experience of safety?

sections.label: Building active upstander culture
sections.summary: The passage asks whether more can be done to build a culture of active upstanders, equipping children to recognise bullying, speak up safely and trust adults to act.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could we do more to build a culture of active upstanders, where children are equipped to recognise bullying, know how to speak up safely and trust that adults will act when concerns are raised?

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the outcome is not whether an incident has been reported, investigated or resolved, but rather, whether the child feels safe again.

sections.label: Equipping parents and listening to children
sections.summary: The passage asks whether parents could be equipped to distinguish healthy challenge from excessive pressure, and whether children could be listened to more systematically about pressure, fear of failure and agency.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, could we equip parents to distinguish healthy developmental challenge from excessive pressure, and to recognise when our understandable aspirations begin to affect a child's well-being or sense of self?

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, could we listen more systematically to children themselves, not only monitoring academic outcomes but understanding their experiences of pressure, fear of failure and agency, and whether they have sufficient space for rest, relationships and exploration?

sections.label: Preschool body safety teaching
sections.summary: Under the Nurturing Early Learners Framework, preschools teach children awareness of safety practices, including body safety and seeking help when hurt or unsafe.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Starting from preschool, under the Nurturing Early Learners Framework, we teach our children to develop awareness of safety practices, including body safety and how to seek help when they feel hurt or unsafe.

sections.label: Common safeguarding baseline suggestion
sections.summary: MOE welcomes Prof Poon's suggestions, including a common safeguarding baseline for organisations that routinely work with children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Beyond these publicly regulated settings, there is value in strengthening safeguarding processes across the broader ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: We welcome Prof Poon's suggestions, including the establishment of a common safeguarding baseline for organisations that routinely work with children.

sections.label: School anti-bullying policy 2027
sections.summary: From 2027, schools will increase reporting channels and support, and all schools will develop an anti-bullying policy under MOE guidelines.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: From 2027, schools will increase the availability and accessibility of reporting channels and support for affected students, and all schools will develop an anti-bullying policy, in accordance with MOE guidelines.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: To further support educators in managing incidents, MOE will continue to strengthen professional development, including training in conflict resolution and parent engagement.

sections.label: Reducing emphasis on academic grades
sections.summary: MOE removed mid-year examinations and moved to the PSLE Achievement Level system, and launched Education Conversations to reduce excessive competition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: That is why MOE has taken decisive steps in recent years to move away from an over-emphasis on academic grades and to nurture in every child the joy of learning throughout life.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: These steps include removing mid-year examinations at all levels and moving to the PSLE Achievement Level system, freeing up more time for students to explore interests beyond the classroom.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: We know that more can, and must be done, and MOE is prepared to review the system broadly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: That is why we launched the Education Conversations in May: to hold open and frank discussions with parents, students and educators on how we can further reduce excessive competition and the over-emphasis on academic achievement.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: MOE will carefully study each of these suggestions, including their merits and trade-offs.

sections.label: Grades as only route narrative
sections.summary: A social narrative persists that good grades are the only route to better opportunities, higher-paying jobs and a good life.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: A deeply held social narrative persists: that good grades are the only route to better opportunities, higher-paying jobs and ultimately, a "good" life.

sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 11.00 am.
